experiment: Geometric attention bias (torsions-in-attention) on PDBbind identity30 -- does the QM9-winning lever help on proteins?
hypothesis: The geometric attention bias (GeometricAttentionBias: E(3)-invariant distance-RBF + flanking bond-angle + dihedral, injected additively into transformer attention logits) was Snir's single best lever on QM9 (~58 meV) but had never been wired into the PDBbind/LBA trainer -- every prior head-to-head used only the weaker walk-PE CONCATENATION of angles/dihedrals. Test whether adding it moves the param-matched transformer past its identity30 parity with GET.
wiring: Added --geom_bias/--emit_xyz/geom_* to quickstart/train_pdbbind.py (trainer-side only; sample_protein_ligand already emits walk_xyz, RSNN_TRSF_Reg already consumes it). +1,444 params -> 693,453 (still matched to GET 719,356, no-bias 692,009). Tests: tests/test_pdbbind_geom_bias.py (8, all pass; full suite 217 passed).
config_under_test: dropout0.1 + geom_bias: --base transformer --h_dim 120 --num_layers 3 --nhead 4 --ffn_mult 4 --reduce mean --pos_enc rope --attn_mode full --lr 1e-3 --dropout 0.1 --m 6 --w 8 --max_len 448 --ligand_max_len 72 --angles 1 --dihedrals 1 --angle_K 8 --dihedral_K 4 --geom_bias 1 --geom_rbf_K 16 --geom_angle_K 8 --geom_dihedral_K 4 --geom_hidden 32. angles/dihedrals kept ON (mirrors QM9 additive use). geom_rbf_cutoff swept in {5,10,15}.
design: Pilot on identity30 only; sweep geom_rbf_cutoff in {5,10,15 A} (QM9 default 5 A is tuned for small molecules; protein pockets span larger). Original plan: select cutoff by VALIDATION Pearson at seed 42, then 3 seeds on the winner. That selection proved too noisy (n=1 val, 466 complexes: val and test ANTI-correlated -- cut15 had best val 0.5648 but worst 3-seed test). So the grid was completed to 3 seeds for EVERY cutoff (dispatch_geom_bias.py full; jobs 68371319 + 68371959).
verdict: NEGATIVE. The geometric attention bias does NOT help on identity30 and DESTABILIZES training. (1) No cutoff reliably beats the no-bias baseline 0.5847: cut5 is nominally +0.014 (0.5982) but with ~3x the variance (+/-0.0345 vs +/-0.0119), a band that fully overlaps the baseline. (2) The cut5 'lead' is an overfit-checkpoint artifact: its two high seeds (0.628, 0.617) come from best_epoch 0 and 2 -- near-untrained checkpoints selected because val RMSE was best at epoch 0 and worsened monotonically as train MSE kept dropping (immediate overfitting on 3507 complexes) -- while the ONE normally-trained cut5 seed (best_epoch 27) scored 0.5499, BELOW baseline. (3) cut10 (0.5442) and cut15 (0.5572) are clearly below baseline. Consistent with the project pattern: on this small dataset dense/simple > structured/complex; added flexibility overfits (cf. param-bump 0.5371, ligand bond-graph 0.5297 with ~5x variance, protein torsion-order 0.5483 -- all hurt). Gate not met (expand only if it beats 0.5847 reliably) -> NOT expanding to identity60/scaffold/LBA.
caveats_and_followups: The best_epoch=0/2 immediate overfitting means the matched recipe (lr 1e-3, dropout 0.1, patience 50) may not be well-suited to the added attention-bias module. A lower-LR / warmup retune of geom_bias is UNTESTED and could in principle stabilize it, but (a) the clean, apples-to-apples comparison is same-recipe, and it says no; (b) the one cut5 seed that did train longer still underperformed. So the negative verdict stands for the matched setting; an LR/warmup retune is a low-priority possible follow-up, not evidence of benefit.
infra: runs/pdbbind_trsf/dispatch_geom_bias.py (Phase A sweep + Phase B selection; 'full' mode = 3-seed grid), sbatch_geom_bias.sh + sbatch_geom_bias_full.sh; outputs runs/pdbbind_trsf/geom_bias/identity30/cut<C>/seed<S>/metrics.json; cutoff_selection.json records the (misleading) val-based pick.
